description: Engagement in cognitively stimulating activities (cognitive training, reading, puzzles, learning). Target of cognitive rehabilitation interventions. Drives neuroplasticity and synaptic function.
Dietary pattern quality (Mediterranean diet adherence, anti-inflammatory diet score). Targets neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, gut-brain axis, and metabolic pathways.
Morning bright light exposure. Target of bright light therapy intervention (threshold model, -0.30 effect at >=20 min/day). Regulates circadian rhythm → sleep quality → HPA axis.

Weekly physical activity level. Primary intervention target for exercise interventions. Dose-response modeled via Emax/Hill functions (EC50 ~200 MET-min/wk for aerobic). Member of Fatigue-Activity feedback loop (LOOP_01).
Self-efficacy for behavior change and intervention adherence. Modulates actual adherence rates (P_adhere in SAFE score). Connected to dopaminergic motivation pathway. Impacted by fatigue and mood.
Sleep quality as a BEHAVIOR (sleep practices, hygiene). Distinct from NODE_SYM_SLEEP_DISRUPTION (the symptom). Target of CBT-I and sleep hygiene interventions. Drives glymphatic clearance pathway.
Social engagement and participation level. Drives cognitive stimulation through social interaction. Impacted by fatigue and depression (C5 pathway). Modulates neuroplasticity.
Active stress management behavior (mindfulness, meditation, relaxation practice). Target of MBSR intervention. Modulates HPA axis and mood pathways.
Urinary or plasma 8-OHdG. Marker of oxidative DNA damage. Proxy for oxidative stress component of OIC composite. Elevated by chemotherapy-induced reactive oxygen species.

PLASMA BDNF (NOT serum — serum levels 20-200x higher due to platelet BDNF, confounding measurement). Primary proxy for neuroplasticity pathway. Increased by exercise, reduced by chronic stress. Anti-correlated with IL-6 (ρ=-0.35).

Salivary cortisol diurnal slope (>=2 days sampling). Flatter/less-negative slope indicates HPA dysregulation (POS_DOWN: higher raw value = flatter = worse). Primary proxy for HPA pathway. Requires multi-timepoint sampling (waking, +30min, afternoon, evening). Correlated with IL-6 (ρ=0.28).
High-sensitivity CRP (serum). Acute phase reactant downstream of IL-6. Less specific to neuroinflammation than IL-6 but more widely available clinically. Correlated with IL-6 (ρ=0.72).
Lymphocyte γ-H2AX foci count by immunofluorescence. Direct marker of DNA double-strand breaks. Elevated by chemotherapy and radiation. Primary proxy for DNA damage pathway.

Fasting blood glucose. Proxy for metabolic dysregulation pathway. Insulin resistance impairs cerebral glucose metabolism and drives neuroinflammation. Elevated by dexamethasone and some chemotherapy regimens.
Plasma IL-6 concentration. Primary peripheral proxy for neuroinflammation (OIC composite). Elevated by chemotherapy, reduced by exercise. Correlated with TNF-α (ρ=0.65), CRP (ρ=0.72).
Plasma malondialdehyde. Lipid peroxidation marker for oxidative stress. Proxy for oxidative stress component of OIC composite. Correlation with IL-6 pending verification.

Plasma neurofilament light chain. Marker of axonal/neuronal damage. CAUTION: Cannot distinguish CNS from PNS damage — elevated in chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy independently of CRCI. Low proxy validity for BBB-specific damage.
T-cell p16^INK4a expression by flow cytometry. Primary peripheral proxy for cellular senescence. Elevated after chemotherapy, especially anthracyclines. Linked to accelerated cognitive aging.

Shannon diversity index from 16S rRNA fecal sequencing. Proxy for gut-brain axis pathway. Reduced by chemotherapy and antibiotics. Limited cancer-specific normative data. Emerging biomarker with low proxy validity.

Plasma TNF-α. Pro-inflammatory cytokine linked to neuroinflammation and SASP (senescence-associated secretory phenotype). Drives cellular senescence pathway. Correlated with IL-6 (ρ=0.65), CRP (ρ=0.58).
Ability to focus on relevant stimuli while filtering distractors. Impaired by anxiety (rumination occupies attentional resources) and neuroinflammation.
Ability to maintain attention over time (vigilance). Commonly impaired in CRCI. Affected by fatigue, sleep disruption, and dopaminergic signaling.
Ability to encode, store, and retrieve new information. Hippocampus-dependent. Most affected by neurogenesis pathway (M5) and BDNF (M4). Commonly reported CRCI complaint.
Executive function: inhibitory control and response suppression. Dependent on prefrontal-striatal circuits. Linked to dopaminergic signaling (M17). Measured by Stroop interference, Go/No-Go.

Executive function: planning, sequencing, and organization. Prefrontal cortex-dependent. Impaired by neuroinflammation-mediated PFC dysfunction. The paper splits executive function into planning and inhibition (2 nodes).

Language comprehension and expression beyond word retrieval (which is verbal fluency). Includes reading comprehension, sentence processing, discourse. Less commonly impaired in CRCI but relevant for functional assessment.
Speed of information processing. MOST SENSITIVE domain to chemotherapy effects (myelin/oligodendrocyte pathway M16). Often first deficit detected. Primary target of TMT-B, Digit Symbol.
Ability to generate words under constraint (phonemic and semantic). Requires processing speed + executive search + semantic memory. Sensitive to white matter integrity (myelin pathway).

Visuospatial processing, construction, and mental rotation. Parietal cortex-dependent. Less commonly reported in CRCI but included for comprehensive cognitive assessment. MoCA includes visuospatial items.
Ability to hold and manipulate information in short-term memory. Affected by neuroinflammation-mediated prefrontal cortex dysfunction. Linked to BDNF/neuroplasticity.

Severity-weighted inverse-variance average across L5 cognitive domains (Formula F-1). Weights w_d = 1/σ²_d. Severity weights 1.0x/1.5x/2.0x at z thresholds 1/2. Six tiers: Excellent(85-100)/Good(70-84)/Mild(50-69)/Moderate(30-49)/Poor(15-29)/Severe(0-14). Score = Φ(-z) × 100.
Age at cancer diagnosis. Modifies neuroplasticity response (BDNF), neurogenesis capacity, and senescence baseline. Grade B modifier for multiple pathways. ACC formula uses max(1,(age-50)/10).
APOE epsilon-4 carrier status. Grade A modifier (Pearce 2022). e4 carriers show attenuated exercise-cognition benefit and amplified neuroinflammatory response to chemotherapy.
Primary cancer diagnosis. Drives prior context matching and cancer-specific pathway activation patterns. Breast cancer has strongest evidence base; others use fallback priors.
Chemotherapy regimen classification (anthracycline, taxane, platinum, alkylating, combination). Primary driver of treatment-induced neurotoxicity across multiple mechanistic pathways.
Premorbid cognitive reserve proxy based on education, occupation, and premorbid IQ. Grade B modifier (Stern 2009). m_CR in [0.7, 1.3]: >16yr edu → 0.7 (protective); <12yr → 1.3 (vulnerability).
Overall comorbidity burden (Charlson Comorbidity Index or count). Modifies metabolic pathway activation and vascular risk. Drives contraindication evaluation for exercise intensity.
Radiation exposure type and location (cranial, whole-body, pelvic, none). Cranial radiation is strongest risk factor for direct CNS damage and BBB disruption.
Biological sex. Modifies HPA axis reactivity and hormonal pathway effects. Relevant for endocrine therapy interactions (tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors).
Current treatment phase. Drives prior selection (33 context-matched matrices) and modifier activation. Key variable for the 4-level fallback hierarchy in ALG-C1.

BBB disruption pathway (M14). EDGELESS PLACEHOLDER. Chemotherapy-induced BBB permeability allows peripheral inflammatory mediators into CNS. NfL is candidate proxy but cannot distinguish CNS from PNS damage. Future expansion candidate.

Cerebrovascular function and perfusion (M11). EDGELESS PLACEHOLDER — pathway concept without parameterized edges in v1. Cerebral blood flow, endothelial function, vascular stiffness. Future expansion candidate.

DNA damage and repair pathway (M7). Direct effect of chemotherapy and radiation. Drives cellular senescence via persistent damage foci. Proxied by γ-H2AX. Moderate-High evidence (1.15x SE multiplier).

Dopaminergic reward and motivation signaling (M17). Chemotherapy may disrupt dopamine synthesis/signaling → reduced motivation → reduced activity engagement → secondary cognitive effects. Low-Moderate evidence (1.75x SE).

Epigenetic modification pathway (M12). Chemotherapy-induced DNA methylation changes, histone modifications affecting gene expression in neuronal and glial cells. Low-Moderate evidence (1.75x SE). No validated peripheral proxy for CNS epigenetic state.

Glymphatic waste clearance (M10). Sleep-dependent CNS waste clearance system. Sleep disruption → impaired glymphatic flow → neuroinflammatory metabolite accumulation. Part of LOOP_05 (HPA→Sleep→Glymphatic→Neuroinflammation→HPA). Low-Moderate evidence (1.75x SE).

Gut-brain axis dysfunction (M8). Chemotherapy-induced dysbiosis → increased intestinal permeability → systemic inflammation → neuroinflammation. Low-Moderate evidence (1.75x SE multiplier). Proxied by Shannon diversity.

Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis dysregulation (M3). NIC covariance structure links this to OIC. Flattened cortisol slope indicates chronic stress response. Drives sleep disruption and mood disturbance. Proxied by cortisol diurnal slope.

Metabolic dysregulation pathway (M13). Insulin resistance, impaired cerebral glucose metabolism. Dexamethasone and hormonal therapy can exacerbate. Links to neuroinflammation via metabolic inflammation. Proxied by fasting glucose.

Myelin and oligodendrocyte integrity (M16). Chemotherapy directly toxic to oligodendrocytes → demyelination → processing speed deficits. Moderate-High evidence (1.15x SE). Primary effect on processing speed domain.

Hippocampal adult neurogenesis (M5). BDNF-dependent. Exercise-promoted, chemotherapy-suppressed. Primary effect on episodic memory. Declines with age. No direct peripheral biomarker; inferred from BDNF + hippocampal volume (imaging).

BDNF-mediated neuroplasticity (M4). Enhanced by exercise, suppressed by chronic inflammation and stress. Key pathway for exercise → cognition benefit. SE multiplier 1.15x (Moderate-High evidence, 1.5x in cancer-specific contexts).

COMPOSITE NODE absorbing M1 (Neuroinflammation) + M2 (Oxidative Stress) + M6 (Mitochondrial Dysfunction). Internal 3x3 covariance matrix + amplification factor α. Resolves bidirectional neuroinflammation ↔ oxidative stress ↔ mitochondrial dysfunction cycle within acyclic DAG. Best proxied by IL-6.

Cellular senescence and SASP (M9). Chemotherapy-induced senescent cell accumulation produces pro-inflammatory secretome. Drives accelerated cognitive aging. Proxied by p16^INK4a. Linked to ACC factor in temporal model.

Synaptic function and long-term potentiation (M15). CONVERGENT HUB — receives input from neuroinflammation, BDNF, metabolic, and other pathways. Final common pathway before cognitive domains. 8 edges. No direct peripheral proxy.
Anxiety symptom severity. Member of LOOP_03 (Anxiety ↔ Sleep, gain=0.11). Driven by HPA dysregulation. Impairs attentional control and working memory through worry/rumination.
Appetite disruption, nausea, weight changes. Chemotherapy-induced. Impacts nutritional status → gut microbiome → metabolic pathways. Particularly relevant during active treatment phase.

Patient-reported cognitive difficulties. Part of CAL covariance structure (correlated with depression — reporting bias). May exceed or underestimate objective cognitive impairment. Important for patient experience but not always correlated with neuropsych testing.

Physical deconditioning and reduced cardiorespiratory fitness. Consequence of treatment-related fatigue → reduced activity → further deconditioning (vicious cycle). Reduced VO2max impairs cerebral blood flow and oxygen delivery.

Depressive symptom severity. Member of LOOP_02 (Depression ↔ Sleep, gain=0.14). Part of CAL covariance structure (Cognitive-Affective Loop) with subjective cognition. PHQ-9 has known somatic confound in cancer (SE 1.5x).

Cancer-related fatigue severity. Most common CRCI comorbid symptom. Member of LOOP_01 (Fatigue ↔ Physical Activity, gain=0.16). Driven by neuroinflammation (OIC) and deconditioning. Directly impairs cognitive performance.
Pain severity (neuropathic and nociceptive). Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy is major contributor. Pain medications (opioids) independently impair cognition. Drives fatigue cycle.

Sleep disruption as SYMPTOM (distinct from NODE_BEH_SLEEP_QUALITY which is the behavior). Insomnia severity, fragmented sleep, non-restorative sleep. Member of LOOP_02 and LOOP_03. Impairs glymphatic clearance. Measured by ISI or PSQI component scores.
